title: Avoozl repository configuration
description: Shareable, non-secret policy stored as .avoozl.json at a repository root. Machine host configuration remains in ~/.config/avoozl/config.json and machine state remains under .avoozl/local.

workspaceId.description: Stable portable identity used when this workspace is registered with a machine host.

namespace.description: Opaque owner of this workspace's GitHub task IDs, written by avoozl init. Managed issue markers carry it; it never changes.

projects.description: Machine-local execution repositories keyed by a stable project ID.

receipts.description: Read by bin/build-receipt in the code repository: `parser` is a command that reads the build output on standard input and prints a JSON object of numbers; `warmCheck` exits 0 when caches are warm. `report` names where build reports (docs/build-report.md) are: a field of each receipt line, or an artifact name prefix.

roles.description: One row per role: its harness, its model where it has one and, for the worker and falsifier, agent. Settings > Models edits it. A missing key or auto keeps the role's default; a task's session pin wins. Older delivery agent and model keys still load into it.

planReview.description: Cross-model draft review. Auto skips review until a reviewer is named and its model can be shown to differ from the writer's.

lanes.description: Worker chats this machine runs at once. Set it in the machine file (~/.config/avoozl/config.json); a value in .avoozl.json is read only when the machine file and delivery.concurrency set none. A ready task beyond the free lanes waits. More lanes come from remote hosts.

landing.description: How Avoozl lands finished work. Who merges and how is each GitHub repository's own landing block.

conflictRounds.description: Older key of each repository's conflicts.maxAttempts, read for a repository that sets none. Still loads; Avoozl does not write it.

trains.description: Ignored. Retired by merge batches: verified work lands in merge batches with landing mode direct. Old files that set it still load.

unionPaths.description: Append-only files merged with union semantics when a landing conflict touches only them.

plugins.description: Plugins this repository declares (design §4.8). A plugin loads only after a person approves its exact version and content hash on each machine. Declare a plugin whose name must stay private in this machine's plugins.json instead.

path.description: A folder relative to this file.

git.description: A repository URL or a local repository path relative to this file. Never a URL with credentials.

ref.description: A tag, branch or full commit. Each machine pins it to one commit when a person adds or updates the plugin.

subdir.description: The plugin's folder inside the git repository.

config.description: Plain, non-secret data for the plugin. A key ending in Env names an environment variable the plugin reads a credential from.

intake.description: Every source that brings work in (design §4.12, §4.39): GitHub repositories (via github, set in Repository setup), intake plugins and MCP callers. Declare a plugin or MCP source whose name must stay private in this machine's plugins.json instead.

via.description: github for a GitHub repository whose issues may start work, plugin:<id> for a plugin that provides intake, or mcp for callers of intake.submit.

repository.description: For github, the owner/name GitHub repository. Otherwise the registered workspace repository whose rules apply and where a delivered item's task lands.

project.description: GitHub sources only: the execution project its work runs in.

workspaceRepository.description: GitHub sources only: the workspace repository, when it is not the project.

label.description: GitHub sources only: the ready label used when the repository has no trigger rules.

assignee.description: GitHub sources only: who the issue must be assigned to.

activity.description: The activity log. retentionDays is how many days rows are kept; each tick deletes older ones.

delivery.description: Turns on readiness dispatch of local leaves by the tick. Limits count sessions the tick opened that have not finished.

concurrency.description: Old input: this machine's lanes when the machine file sets no lanes.local. Use lanes.local in the machine file.

model.description: The worker's model. Review roles with distinctFrom model must differ from it.

runner.description: Who starts worker sessions for ready leaves: the tick's script cron, or a Crew Mode conductor that claims them through avoozl next and claim. The tick verifies and integrates either way.

prFeedback.description: Send a pull request's review comments and failed checks back to the worker.

ship.description: Older key of each GitHub repository's landing.autoMerge (design 4.25), read for a repository that sets none. manual means false. Still loads; Avoozl does not write it.

concurrency.description: Ignored. lanes.local in the machine file is the one limit for chats.

ship.description: Older key of the repository's landing.autoMerge. Still loads; Avoozl does not write it.

repositories.description: One repository's own delivery settings, by project ID, over the workspace's.

contentRules.description: Content rule sets (design 4.9). The rules themselves live in a terms file outside Git or in a rules plugin, never here.

claimStaleAfter.description: When a worker's claim shows in Needs you: like "90m", "24h" or "2d", or a number of seconds.

packs.description: Written by a pack import (design §4.14): for each plugin whose pack was imported, the version and time of the import and the settings that came from it. Records provenance only; Avoozl never re-applies it.

notifications.description: Where this machine sends notifications when no Kiro Crew does. Machine file only (~/.config/avoozl/config.json): .avoozl.json refuses it, since a webhook URL may hold a secret.

serve.description: Run the standalone page under this machine's supervisor. Global configuration only; the repository file may not set it.

machine.description: This machine's settings. Global configuration only.

platforms.description: Ignored. Retired by merge batches: verified work lands in merge batches with landing mode direct. Old files that set it still load.

slots.description: Ignored. Retired by merge batches: verified work lands in merge batches with landing mode direct. Old files that set it still load.

lease.description: Ignored. Retired by merge batches: verified work lands in merge batches with landing mode direct. Old files that set it still load.

commandSink.description: Runs an argument list, never a shell, with the title and the small JSON payload appended.

webhookSink.description: Posts the small JSON payload once to an https URL, or http to this machine.

runner.description: Worker mode, off unless role is set. A worker pulls its own offers from spec journals. Machine paths (repos) belong in ~/.config/avoozl/config.json.

executor.description: What runs the session: a Kiro Crew chat, or a process child of the supervisor.

workerMode.description: How an unattended worker's tool calls are approved. Off unless set.

pools.description: Worker role: the spec journals this worker pulls offers from.

sources.description: Worker role: the source repositories this worker may fetch, by owner/name.

lanes.description: Worker role: how many tasks this worker runs at once.

portablePath.description: A path relative to the repository root. Absolute machine paths belong in ~/.config/avoozl/config.json.

autoArchiveCompleted.description: Archive completed child and task conversations while retaining their task and transcript links.

checks.description: The repository's checks: a check name to its command arguments, or to {run, paths}. A check with paths runs only for a change that touches one of them. Every task runs these; tasks never name checks. An older list of argument arrays still loads, each check named by its command.

checksEnv.description: Names of environment variables the checks may read.

worktreeHelper.description: SHA-256 hash of the approved worktree helper script.

landing.description: How verified work reaches the base branch. direct: Avoozl lands verified work on the base in merge batches. pr: Avoozl opens a pull request and merges it once its checks pass. train: retired; it loads as direct. off, or absent: Avoozl pushes nothing and the commit waits for a person.

planning.description: This repository contributes Markdown planning documents.

editable.description: Agents may create worktrees and prepare changes in this checkout.

executor.description: What runs this project's sessions: a Kiro Crew chat, or a process child of the supervisor.

harness.description: The harness definition a process session uses.

isolation.description: How the repository's checks run. A person sets it in Settings > Repository setup.

run.description: sandbox: the process sandbox, writing only the check's folder, its temp and cache folders and the writable paths. container: docker or podman with image. unconfined: no isolation, only with this machine's opt-in.

image.description: The container image, needed when run is container.

network.description: Whether a check reaches the network.

readable.description: Absolute paths a check may also read.

writable.description: Absolute paths a check may also write.

prepare.description: A command run once per worktree and commit before its checks, outside isolation, such as npm ci.

sandbox.description: What a process session may write, run and reach.

writeRoots.description: Absolute folders the session may write besides its worktree. Never the home folder, the filesystem root or the git directory.

allowCommands.description: Commands the session may run without asking, each an argv list of plain words. git push is never allowed.

network.description: off, or the localhost ports the session may reach.

flow.description: This repository's own flow settings, over the workspace's. Settings > Flow writes it.

github.description: Desired non-secret GitHub configuration: mode, task authority, Project, and per-repository policy (design §4.4), Remote setup remains an explicit action.

mode.description: Where issues live. local, or absent, means every task is local; GitHub settings stored beside local are kept but not used. Derived from repository roles when any repository has a role.

planningRepository.description: Planning repository for plans-repo mode; kept but not used in other modes.

defaultAuthority.description: Authority of new tasks. Defaults to github when a mode is set, else local.

cacheSeconds.description: How long GitHub answers stay fresh, in seconds. Inside it Avoozl makes no GitHub call for a read. 0 turns the cache off. A repository may set its own.

writesPerMinute.description: The most GitHub writes Avoozl makes in a minute.

writesPerHour.description: The most GitHub writes Avoozl makes in an hour.

maxPerParent.description: How many sub-issues Avoozl links under one parent issue. GitHub's own limit is 100.

includeDone.description: Whether a task already done when its spec is approved gets an issue.

specReviewers.description: The GitHub logins asked to review each spec's approval pull request, by spec folder name. With none, the repository's own CODEOWNERS and rules decide.

avoozlState.description: Single-select field Avoozl fills with its Delivery state. Blank: Avoozl skips it.

phase.description: Text field Avoozl fills with each task's phase.

statusValues.description: Project Status option names. Only deferred is read as an order.

githubRepositoryPolicy.description: Who may trigger work in one repository and which labels do what. No label name is built in.

role.description: What this repository is for (design §4.34). local: tasks stay in the workspace database. code: pull requests land here and issues live in the planning repository. planning: holds the issues and specs, no code. both: code and its own issues. The mode and planningRepository derive from the roles.

baseBranch.description: Must equal the repository's default branch when a mode is set.

radar.description: Avoozl's workflow labels. Planning, needs-human, claim, ready, conflict, approval, review and drafted names must all differ.

escalationDraft.description: Draft a trusted Issue Radar escalation's bounded-fix acceptance locally when the needs-human label appears. Writes nothing to GitHub; a person still starts it.

showPlansRepo.description: Show the plans repository name in issues. Unset: on for a private code repository, off for a public one.

reviewRules.description: Review rules Set up proposes for AGENTS.md in a pull request. Unset: the built-in rules.

crew.description: What Set up shows for an Issue Radar crew. Avoozl creates no crew.

count.description: Batch size: how many crews Set up shows. Not a concurrency setting.

pullRequestReviews.description: GitHub pull request reviews as a leaf's review verdict. Present means on.

approvals.description: How many allowed approvals the head commit needs.

conflicts.description: What Avoozl does with a conflict: merges the base in and fixes it, or only asks a person.

maxAttempts.description: Tries per conflict before a person is asked, for landing conflicts sent back to the worker chat and for crew pull requests. Unset reads landing.conflictRounds.

landing.description: Who merges and how, for this repository (design 4.25). Edited on Settings > Repository setup > Edit > Landing.

mode.description: How Avoozl lands verified work. Unset reads the checkout's projects.<id>.landing, else off.

autoMerge.description: true: the writer turns on GitHub auto-merge. false: a person merges. Unset reads delivery.ship.

method.description: How a pull request merges. Unset reads merge.method.

mergeBatch.description: direct landing: how many verified tasks land in one merge batch. auto sizes the batch from how often changes fail; a number from 1 to 16 replaces the size, and 1 lands one task at a time.

merge.description: Older key of landing.method. Still loads; Avoozl does not write it.

cacheSeconds.description: This repository's GitHub cache time in seconds, instead of github.cacheSeconds.

release.description: Ready-label capacity: N at once per repository, and per crew label scope. N defaults to 1; 0 releases nothing. With lanes, the only concurrency setting.

mode.description: Automatic releases as slots free. Step waits for one click per phase. Hold releases nothing; a person adds the ready label by hand.

ranking.description: Which eligible task gets the ready label next: the one that unblocks most first, a task whose paths overlap claimed work or an open pull request held back, and a held task moved up after each agingHours wait. Only the order changes.

buildReceipts.description: The code repository has bin/build-receipt. Each issue brief then tells crews to run build and test commands through it.

priorityLabels.description: Labels in priority order. They order tasks inside Ready and Up next, never the lane. The newer name for priority; set only one of the two.

waitingLabels.description: Labels that mean the item waits on someone outside, such as response-requested. A task whose item has one waits in Blocked or waiting with the reason Waiting on the author.

managedLabels.description: Labels Avoozl adds and removes. Each must differ from every trigger label.

crewLabels.description: Issue Radar's own labels, which Avoozl reads and never writes.

decisionRecord.description: Add a decision record to the approval pull request.

acceptedLabel.description: A label an allowed actor adds to say a skipped issue may be planned.

commentSteering.description: Relay a comment that names mention, by an allowed actor, to the running leaf's worker. Off unless present.

discussions.description: Answer discussions in these categories whose author is allowed. Off unless present.

triage.description: The triage agent for this repository: it answers, reproduces, fixes and reviews new issues and pull requests.

existing.description: Whether the agent takes the open items already there when it is turned on, or only new ones.

untriaged.description: What the Triage list shows for this repository.

filter.description: A GitHub search line that narrows the list.

githubRule.description: Matches when its match line holds, or when every labelsAll label, one labelsAny label (when given), no labelsNone label, and the assignee and author hold, and the newest event that made it true came from an allowed actor.

match.description: A GitHub search line, such as label:bug no:assignee. It replaces labelsAll, labelsAny, labelsNone and assignee; a rule sets match or those, never both, and needs at least one positive label either way.

githubMirror.description: Crews work a private mirror of a public repository; Avoozl forwards finished work to the source.

mirror.description: The private mirror. It must differ from source.

forward.description: auto needs at least one trusted person.

plansBranch.description: Must differ from the default branch and not start with branchPrefix.

forwardExclude.description: Relative paths or patterns never forwarded, such as docs/private/ or **/*.pem.

githubLabelBehaviors.description: Repository-specific GitHub labels mapped to normalized Avoozl Queue states. Omitted behaviors use the avoozl:* defaults.

flow.description: Flow settings: what a failure stops, when a retro runs, what counts as CI waste, and what verification protects. The retro instructions are saved on each machine, never here.

scope.description: What a failed check on the base stops: the tasks that depend on it, its repository, or all new work.

localChecksFirst.description: Run the declared checks locally before pushing.

model.description: The older place for the retro's model; models.retro wins.

ci.description: What counts as steady CI waste.

classes.description: Path globs for each file class of a pull request's changed paths. A class's list replaces the built-in one.

protectedPaths.description: Path globs a worker's commit may not change, beyond the built-in ones. A repository adds to the workspace's list.

checkTimeouts.description: A check's name to its own timeout in seconds. A key written as the check's command still matches.

deliveryInvestigate.description: Investigate before coding (design 4.21): the worker reports findings, a falsifier tries to refute them, and coding starts only at minConfidence.

deliveryReviewer.description: One review role for a finished pull request. With distinctFrom model, its model must be named and differ from delivery.model.
